name: Sort objects into groups
description: Student can sort a collection of objects into groups.
exampleOfSuccess: The student sorts toy animals into farm animals and sea animals.
commonError: Student sorts inconsistently or makes groups that overlap.
checkpointTask: Give the student a collection. Ask them to sort it into groups and name each group.

name: Collect data to answer a question
description: Student can collect simple data to answer a given yes or no question.
exampleOfSuccess: To answer 'Do you have a pet?', the student collects a yes or no from each person.
commonError: Student collects answers that do not match the question, or asks only some people.
checkpointTask: Pose a simple yes or no question. Ask the student to collect the answers from the group.

name: Organise data with objects or pictures
description: Student can organise collected data using objects or pictures.
exampleOfSuccess: The student lines up a block for each 'yes' and each 'no' in two rows.
commonError: Student piles the data together so the groups cannot be compared.
checkpointTask: Give the student collected data. Ask them to organise it using objects or pictures.

name: Compare the groups
description: Student can compare the groups in their data and say which has more or fewer.
exampleOfSuccess: Looking at the two rows, the student says more people said yes than no.
commonError: Student compares by which row looks longer without checking the counts.
checkpointTask: Show the student organised data. Ask which group has more and which has fewer.

name: Answer the question from the data
description: Student can use the sorted data to answer the original question.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 'most of us have a pet, because the yes row is longer'.
commonError: Student describes the data but does not connect it back to the question asked.
checkpointTask: After the student organises data, ask what it tells them about the original question.
